            @media (max-width: 900px) {
              .mw-landing .pillars { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }

              .mw-landing .mw-section { padding: 3.5rem 1rem; }

              .mw-landing .pillar:hover, .mw-landing .book-card:hover { transform: none; }

  <h1>Every migration is a <em>governance</em> migration.</h1>

<section class="mw-section" id="approach">
  <div class="mw-inner">
    <p class="section-label">How Every Book Works</p>
    <h2 class="section-title">One question. Four parts. Every claim sourced.</h2>
    <p class="section-body">Each book takes one modernization topic and answers the same four questions in order. Every external fact is checked against a primary source (Microsoft Learn, NIST, OMB, CISA, FedRAMP, the IETF) and footnoted, the diagrams share one house style, and each book comes with a Word edition and a 15-minute presentation.</p>
    <div class="pillars">
      <div class="pillar">
        <div class="pillar-label">Why</div>
        <h3>Why the topic matters now.</h3>
        <p>The opening question each book answers, and the mandate, risk or loss that makes it urgent.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="pillar what">
        <div class="pillar-label">What</div>
        <h3>What changes, and what replaces it.</h3>
        <p>What the old system quietly did, what the target architecture is, and the decisions that carry the risk.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="pillar who">
        <div class="pillar-label">Who</div>
        <h3>Who decides, and who does the work.</h3>
        <p>Owners, approvers and operators, with the separation of duties the controls expect.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="pillar how">
        <div class="pillar-label">How</div>
        <h3>How to migrate, operate and evidence it.</h3>
        <p>Phased migration with rollback at every step, day-two operations, and the evidence an assessor will ask for.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="mw-section band" id="problem">
  <div class="mw-inner problem-grid">
    <div>
      <p class="section-label">The Problem</p>
      <h2 class="section-title">Active Directory did more governance than anyone wrote down.</h2>
    </div>
    <div>
      <p class="section-body">For twenty years the directory quietly decided who existed, what a computer received, which certificates were trusted and where names resolved. Moving to the cloud removes that machinery, and each piece fails in its own way, often long after the cutover is declared done. Each book takes one of those pieces.</p>
      <ul class="problem-list">
        <li><span>Identity lifecycle driven by IT tickets instead of the HR system of record. <a href="docs/books/b03-hr-identity/index.html">Book 03</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Access decisions scattered across groups, roles and exceptions with no single policy. <a href="docs/books/b04-access/index.html">Book 04</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Group Policy targeting by OU position, which nothing in Intune reads. <a href="docs/books/b05-devices/index.html">Book 05</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Windows Authentication and NTLM hidden inside the database estate. <a href="docs/books/b06-data-platform/index.html">Book 06</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Certificates that keep working after cutover, until the first expiry finds no issuer. <a href="docs/books/b07-pki/index.html">Book 07</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Split-brain DNS that surfaces as certificate errors and access denials. <a href="docs/books/b08-ddi/index.html">Book 08</a></span></li>
        <li><span>Field offices that hairpin through a distant data center, or break out to the internet before the governor is live. <a href="docs/books/b09-network/index.html">Book 09</a></span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

    <h2 class="section-title">All eighteen books published.</h2>

      <h2 class="section-title">"Show your work."</h2>
      <p class="section-body">In May 2025 the U.S. Federal Chief Information Officer, Gregory J. Barbaccia, sent federal technology leaders sixteen operating principles. They are the standard this workbook tries to meet.</p>
      <div class="hero-actions" style="justify-content:flex-start;margin-top:1.5rem;">
        <a class="btn-primary" href="docs/inspiration/index.html">Read the principles</a>

    </div>
    <div>
      <ul class="problem-list">
        <li><span><b>Show your work.</b> Every claim in the workbook is checked against a primary source and footnoted, and each book keeps its verification log beside its chapters.</span></li>
        <li><span><b>Truth over comfort.</b> When a source turns out to be wrong or out of date, the books say so and correct it in the open.</span></li>
        <li><span><b>Label the problem.</b> Every book names the governance Active Directory quietly did before it proposes what replaces it.</span></li>
        <li><span><b>Cross-functional thinking is mandatory.</b> Identity, devices, data, certificates, DNS and the network are treated as one system.</span></li>
      </ul>
